paper_metadata.title: NCERT Class 7 Science Chapter 3 Model Test Paper
instructions: Section A contains 6 Objective Questions (4 MCQs + 2 Assertion-Reason) carrying 1 Mark each.
Section B contains 5 Short Answer Questions carrying 2 Marks each.
Section C contains 2 Long Answer Questions carrying 4 Marks each.
Section D contains 1 Case-Based Competency Question with 3 sub-questions carrying 2 Marks each.

questions.question_text: Current flows through an LED regardless of which lead connects to the positive cell terminal.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct option selection (B). Explanation: LEDs are unidirectional semiconductor devices that conduct current only in forward bias (longer lead to positive).

questions.question_text: What is the key scientific indicator or property studied in Chapter 3?
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct option selection (A). Explanation: Derived from core terms.

questions.question_text: Which process occurs during the core phenomenon in Electricity: Circuits and their Components?
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct option (C). Explanation: Standard curriculum observation.

questions.question_text: Select the correct definition for 'Electric Current Direction':
options: A) Conventional current flows from the positive (+) terminal of the power source to the negative (-) terminal.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct option (A). Explanation: Definition of Electric Current Direction as stated in NCERT textbook.

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Electric current flows through a circuit only when the switch is in the closed (ON) position.
Reason (R): A closed switch provides a continuous, unbroken path of conducting material.
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) (A) is true but (R) is false.
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct selection (A). Explanation: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Electricians wear rubber gloves while handling live wires.
Reason (R): Rubber is a good conductor of electricity.
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) (A) is true but (R) is false.
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct selection (C). Explanation: (A) is true but (R) is false. Rubber is an insulator.

questions.question_text: Contrast incandescent bulbs and LEDs regarding energy efficiency and heat generation.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Incandescent bulbs generate light by heating a filament to high temperatures, wasting significant energy as heat. LEDs convert electrical energy directly into light with minimal heat waste.
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for identifying first key point; 1 Mark for second key point / clear explanation.

questions.question_text: A student builds a simple circuit with a cell, switch, and bulb, but the bulb fails to glow when the switch is closed. List five potential faults.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Dead/discharged electric cell. 2. Fused bulb filament. 3. Loose wire connections at terminals. 4. Broken internal wire conductor. 5. Oxidation/rust on contact points.
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for statement/formula; 1 Mark for calculation/application.
1 Mark for Point 1 of difference; 1 Mark for Point 2 of difference.

questions.question_text: Why must electric cells in a multi-cell torch be connected positive-terminal-to-negative-terminal?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Series connection (+ to -) combines the individual voltage potentials of the cells, driving sufficient electromotive force through the filament to produce bright light. Connecting like terminals (+ to +) cancels potential.
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for identifying core cause; 1 Mark for explaining scientific effect.

questions.question_text: Correct the common misconception: 'Believing electric current is consumed or destroyed inside the bulb filament.'. Provide the correct scientific fact.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Electric current is not consumed; electrical energy is converted into thermal and radiant light energy while charge continues flowing back to the negative terminal.
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for identifying error; 1 Mark for stating correct scientific fact.

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer Questions - Diagrams & Processes)

questions.question_text: Explain how an LED works, detail lead identification rules, and draw schematic circuit diagrams for functional (forward-biased) and non-functional (reverse-biased) LED circuits.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: An LED is a polar semiconductor light source. Lead identification: Longer lead = Positive (+) Anode; Shorter lead = Negative (-) Cathode. Forward-Biased Circuit: Longer lead connected to cell positive terminal, shorter lead to switch and cell negative terminal; LED glows bright. Reverse-Biased Circuit: Longer lead connected to cell negative terminal; current is blocked and LED remains dark.
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for introduction/definition; 2 Marks for detailed 4-point mechanism; 1 Mark for conclusion/example.

questions.question_text: Explain the structure and operation illustrated in 'Fig. 3.5 / Circuit Symbols Set'. (i) Draw/describe the key components (Cell (Long/Short line), Battery, Bulb, LED (Triangle with arrows), Switch ON/OFF, Wire). (ii) Detail the working mechanism and scientific significance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Component breakdown: Cell (Long/Short line), Battery, Bulb, LED (Triangle with arrows), Switch ON/OFF, Wire.
Mechanism & Significance: Provides standardized visual representation for designing and analyzing electric circuits.
questions.breakdown: 2 Marks for labeling/describing key components accurately; 2 Marks for explaining working mechanism clearly.

question.case_scenario_text: An electrician uses rubber gloves and plastic-handled pliers while repairing household electrical switches.

sub_questions.question_text: Why are rubber and plastic used on electrical repair tools?
sub_questions.marking_scheme_answer: Rubber and plastic are electrical insulators (poor conductors) that prevent electric current from flowing through the tools into the human body, preventing electric shocks.
sub_questions.breakdown: 2 Marks for complete, accurate identification/explanation of the initial phenomenon.

sub_questions.question_text: Formulate a testable hypothesis or identify the chemical/physical principle.
sub_questions.breakdown: 2 Marks for correct scientific reasoning and principle formulation.

sub_questions.question_text: What conclusion or practical precaution can be derived from this experimental observation?
sub_questions.marking_scheme_answer: Practical conclusion and safety/precautionary measure grounded in textbook guidelines.
sub_questions.breakdown: 2 Marks for valid evidence-based conclusion / real-world application.
